paras: The killing of Ed Walls was the fatal shooting of a Black man by a police officer, A. L. Brookins, at 111 South Thirty-ninth street, apparently in Birmingham, Alabama, at about 1:40 a.m. on August 16, 1915. Walls had just been arrested on a woman's complaint, and the only report, in the Birmingham Age-Herald, gave the officers' account that he seized a pistol and fired before he was shot.

According to the Age-Herald, Katie Myers, a Black woman, complained to police headquarters that Walls was trying to kill her and asked the officers to arrest him. Officers Brookins and J. A. Ellard were sent on the call.

The officers placed Walls under arrest when they reached the address, and Brookins started for the patrol. In the version the paper printed, Walls then jumped at Ellard's throat from behind and wrenched the pistol from his hand. Walls was said to have fired twice at Ellard, one bullet lodging in the padding of his coat and the other passing between his legs. Brookins turned as Walls was pulling the trigger a third time and shot him in the abdomen, a wound that "proved fatal."
No report of an inquest, an inquiry into the shooting, or any statement by Myers or other witnesses appears in the coverage found.

The Birmingham Age-Herald ran the story the same morning on page 8 under the headline "Negro Shot While Resisting Arrest." Its opening sentence called Walls "a negro desperado," and the item related the officers' account as fact, without attribution and without any other version. The paper spelled his name both "Walls" and "Wall."
No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have reported the shooting, so the event rests on this single police-sourced item.

reader.title: Killing of Ed Walls
bases: A city police officer shot and killed Walls while he was under arrest; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
One local white newspaper item, which gives only the police version, is the sole report found in either press (A1).
